newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up task-force to prepare referendum.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up task-force to prepare referendum.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Sunday set up a task-force headed by his Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia to prepare for a referendum on amending the country's constitution within the next three months.
"The Algerian people will have the chance to express their choice on constitutional revision, in conditions of security, freedom and transparency," said Zeroual.
He was quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS as addressing a cabinet meeting he chaired at the presidential palace in Algiers.

The referendum, a first milestone in Zeroual's planned political reforms to reshape the country's future, will be followed by general elections in the first half of 1997 and local polls in the second half of next year.

Zeroual seeks to cut the ground from beneath both radical Islamists and their hardline secularist foes by pinning in the amended constitution that Islam is the nation's religion, protected and promoted only by the state.

Government forces and Moslem rebels have been locked in conflict since January 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. About 50,000 people have since been killed.
The authorities accuse Moslem militants of hijacking the Moslem faith to try to win power.
The amended constitution, among other issues, will limit the president to two terms in office and create a high court able to try the head of the state and the prime minister for treason.
Zeroual told a news conference on Saturday the government has alredy "achieved great deal of progress" in laying the ground for the referendum.
He said the referendum would be marked by the same freedom and security as was the presidential election last November.
Then, more than 100,000 police and troops threw a security blanket across the country to guard more than 13 million voters in the face of Moslem rebel threats to kill those who voted.
